title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
why: The first computer to beat a reigning world chess champion in a match.

title: Watson wins Jeopardy!
why: Beats Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter on national TV.

title: AlexNet wins ImageNet
why: A GPU-trained neural net crushes computer vision's main benchmark. The deep learning era starts here.

title: DQN learns Atari from pixels
why: One network learns dozens of games from the screen alone.

title: GANs
why: Two networks competing to fake and detect images. The root of AI image generation.

title: ResNet
why: 152-layer networks beat human-level accuracy on ImageNet.

title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
why: Wins the Go match a decade before experts expected. Move 37 becomes famous.

title: Attention Is All You Need
why: The Transformer paper. Every modern LLM is built on it.

title: AlphaGo Zero
why: Masters Go from scratch with no human games, then beats AlphaGo 100-0.

title: AlphaZero beats Stockfish
why: Teaches itself chess in hours and beats the strongest engine.

title: BERT
why: Pre-trained Transformers take over language understanding.

title: AlphaFold wins CASP13
why: First place in the protein structure prediction contest on its first try.

title: AlphaStar beats StarCraft pros
why: Beats professional players at a real-time strategy game.

title: GPT-2
why: Writes coherent paragraphs. OpenAI calls it too dangerous to release in full.

title: OpenAI Five beats the Dota 2 champions
why: Beats OG, the reigning world champions.

title: GPT-3
why: 175 billion parameters. Learns new tasks from a few examples in the prompt.

title: AlphaFold 2
why: Effectively solves protein structure prediction, a 50-year-old problem in biology.

title: DALL·E and CLIP
why: Images from text prompts. The avocado armchair.

title: GitHub Copilot
why: AI autocomplete for code ships to developers.

title: AlphaFold maps the human proteome
why: Predicted structures for nearly every human protein, released free.

title: DALL·E 2
why: Photorealistic images from a sentence.

title: Stable Diffusion
why: A strong image model with open weights that runs on a home GPU.

title: ChatGPT
why: The fastest-growing consumer app ever. 100 million users in two months.

title: GPT-4
why: Scores in the top 10% on the bar exam.

title: Sora
why: Minute-long, photorealistic video from text.

title: GPT-4o voice
why: Real-time voice that laughs, sings and gets interrupted.

title: AlphaProof wins IMO silver
why: Silver-medal level at the International Math Olympiad.

title: o1 reasons before it answers
why: The first reasoning model. Thinking longer makes it smarter.

title: AI wins two Nobel Prizes
why: Physics for neural networks, then chemistry for AlphaFold.

title: Claude uses a computer
why: An AI that moves the mouse, clicks and types.

title: o3 cracks ARC-AGI
why: 87.5% on a benchmark built to resist AI.

title: DeepSeek-R1
why: An open reasoning model that matches o1 at a fraction of the cost. Nvidia loses about $590B a week later.

title: Deep Research
why: Writes analyst-grade research reports in minutes.

title: Claude Code
why: Agentic coding moves into the terminal.

title: GPT-4o image generation
why: Studio Ghibli everything. The internet melts.

title: AlphaEvolve
why: Finds new algorithms, beating a 56-year-old matrix multiplication record.

title: Veo 3 adds sound
why: AI video with dialogue, sound effects and music.

title: AI wins IMO gold
why: Gold-medal scores at the International Math Olympiad.

title: Genie 3
why: Interactive worlds generated in real time.

title: Claude codes for 30 hours
why: Sonnet 4.5 works on its own for 30 hours straight.

title: Claude beats every human on Anthropic's exam
why: Opus 4.5 outscores every candidate on the engineering take-home.

title: GPT-6 Astra
why: Pitched as able to do anything you can do on a computer.

title: Navier–Stokes solution claimed
why: About 10,000 agents produce a Lean-formalized solution to a Millennium Prize problem.

title: Claude Opus 5 out-works accountants
why: Does a human accountant's work in 10 minutes.

title: 700+ AI-written math papers
why: A Fields Medalist says it "annihilated my research area."
